chunk_findings.detail: The re-check compares `last["code_proof"]` with `last["code_hash"]`, but `code_hash` is the stored hash that the verifier itself reads from the ask state. A forger who can hand-append an `ask.answered` line can set `source` to any allowed non-terminal word (e.g. `"web"`) and set `code_proof` equal to a copy of `last["code_hash"]`; `hmac.compare_digest` then compares the stored hash with itself and passes without the forger ever knowing the one-time code. Example: for an ask with `last["code_hash"] == "abc..."`, append `{"kind":"ask.answered","id":A,"human":true,"source":"web","code_proof":"abc...","coded":true,"digest":D,"answered_digest":D,"outcome":"yes"}`; `verdict` approves. So non-terminal forgeries still pass, not just the acknowledged `source=terminal` limit.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/engine.py:279 (verdict code-proof re-check)

chunk_findings.detail: When the ask has no one-time code (`last["code_hash"]` is empty), the code-proof branch is skipped entirely. A hand-appended answer with any non-terminal `source` in `ANSWER_SOURCES` and `human=True` therefore passes: the source check only tests membership in a word list, and there is no code to compare. Example: for a no-code ask with digest `D`, append `{"kind":"ask.answered","id":A,"human":true,"source":"web","code_proof":"","coded":false,"digest":D,"answered_digest":D,"outcome":"yes"}`; `verdict` returns True. This is outside the acknowledged terminal-source limit and approves a forged non-terminal answer without any secret.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ask/engine.py:277 (verdict no-code path)

chunk_findings.detail: The change still does not satisfy its stated guarantee that `verdict` must not approve a hand-appended `ask.answered`. The intent itself records the bypass: a forged answer with `source="terminal"` and the same uid/L1 identity is approved. For example, for a plain ask (`with_code=False`), a log writer in the same uid can append an `ask.answered` event containing `source="terminal"` and the matching identity fields; `verdict` will return `ok`, even though the answer was never produced through `engine.answer`. The new tests in `tests/test_ask_engine_forged_answer.py` do not exercise this case, so the suite passes while the forged terminal answer remains accepted.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `if last["source"] not in ANSWER_SOURCES:` check makes every `ask.answered` event written before this change fail verification. `ddflow/core/handlers/asks.py:78` now parses a missing `source` field as `""`, and old answer events have no `source` key at all. For an already-answered ask recorded before this change, `verdict` therefore reaches that line with `last["source"] == ""` and returns `False` with "the answer carries no recorded source", even when the answer is genuine, the digests match, and there was no one-time code to prove. No migration or fallback to the old per-answer fields (for example `via`) is added, so upgrading with existing answered asks breaks their decisions.

chunk_findings.detail: The only new no-code forged-answer test is vacuous for the no-code bypass it is meant to guard. `test_an_answer_without_a_recorded_source_does_not_approve` forges an `ask.answered` line with no `source`, but the previously reported no-code exploit requires an allowed non-terminal `source` such as `"web"` or `"terminal"` together with `human=True`; without `source`, the old no-code branch already rejected or returned not-ok. The input that actually still passes on a no-code ask (forged answer with `source="terminal"`, `human=True`, `coded=False`) is not tested, so this test gives false confidence while the engine’s stated guarantee remains unmet for plain asks.

<result>Both bugs are closed and the fix is on main (merge `14c77725`). Bed643a611b was completed through `ddflow complete`. Bb305b43f56 was closed with `ddflow bug fixed`, but its task `fix-Bb305b43f56` is released, not completed. My event log is committed and nothing is ahead of main.

**Bed643a611b (hand-recorded passes on command gates)**
- **Root cause:** `gate record` had no check on command gates, so an agent could type a command and exit code and get a green `unit_tests` or `ci`. The report's `by_hand` check also treated a bare `command` key as proof a tool ran.
- **Fix:** an agent's hand `--outcome passed` on a command gate is now refused with exit 3. Agent means `--agent`, `DDFLOW_AGENT`, `CLAUDECODE`, or MCP.
  - **Still allowed:** `unavailable`, `partial`, `gate skip`, `gate run`, `ci run`, and a person at a terminal.
  - **`ci run`:** it is marked with an internal `ran_by` field that no CLI flag or MCP argument can set, and only known values count.
  - **After a real run:** I removed my earlier "unless a real run exists" allowance, since a second typed pass would overwrite the run's evidence.
  - **Report:** `by_hand` now counts `command_digest` or a known `ran_by`, not a bare command string.
- **Regression test:** `tests/test_gate_record_by_hand_command.py`. It failed against the unfixed code (`assert 0 == 3`).
- **Mutation:** making `handrecord._refusal` always return `""` fails 3 tests.
- **Tests I had to adjust:** some existing tests hand-record command gates under the agent harness, so I made them record as a person. These are `test_gate_output_evidence`, `test_gate_run_after_merge`, `test_gate_econ_tests`, `test_tests_selection_report` and `test_scenarios`.

**Bb305b43f56 (what a hand record did not measure)**
- A hand record now stores `output_file_host` (the recording agent) and an `unmeasured` list. The list names `tree_sha` when no tree was measured, and `elapsed_s` and `command_digest` when a command was typed.
- Regression test: `tests/test_gate_record_measured_fields.py`. It failed before the change with `KeyError: 'unmeasured'`.
- It was fixed by the same merge. I skipped its own gates with reasons pointing at the sibling item, because it has no separate diff, and recorded research normally.
- `ddflow complete fix-Bb305b43f56` refused without `--force`, which I did not use. Skipped `implement`, `unit_tests` and `merge` do not count as passed, and no reviewer had run on that item.
- The bug close itself ran with `[could-not-run]`: ddflow could not check the test against pre-fix source without a worktree.

**Gates on fix-Bed643a611b**
- Passed: research, rules, implement, rubber_duck, critic, standards, ci, unit_tests, bug_hunt, dedupe, merge.
- **Reviewer:** deepseek (lan-deepseek-v4-pro) for rubber_duck and critic, with roborev job 3251 for standards. Different model family from me.
- **Rounds used:** rubber_duck 4 of 4 and critic 4 of 4. No fifth round was needed.
- **Passed on refutation:** critic only (5 refuted, 2 confirmed).
- **Unseen by a reviewer:** several commits after the last review rounds:
  - removing the "after a real run" allowance;
  - the `CI_RUN` constant;
  - the `test_tests_selection_report` and `test_scenarios` fixtures.
- **Standards:** recorded against sha `1fd264e`, not the final head, so roborev has not seen the later changes.
- **ci:** passed on the second attempt after main's fixes landed.

**For the operator**
- Any workflow where an agent hand-records a command gate is now refused. Projects that configure a command for `standards` or `docs` get this too, so they must use `gate run`.
- `complete` printed notes that critic, rubber_duck and standards passed on a different tree than what landed, and that the README was not updated. I did not re-run them.

**Defects filed**
- B1fa77a6832: the `ci run` lock has no FIFO, so `gate run ci` starved for hours. Five attempts were recorded `unavailable`, one of them a 3600s timeout.
- B978b5c4772: `test_worktree_adoption` was red on main. Another agent fixed it as Bbcba9046fc.
- B512cbb5b88: `test_mcp_parity` was red on main for `ddflow_complete` and `ddflow_bug_fixed`. It was fixed on main.</result>

chunk_findings.detail: The completeness check is only module-granularity. `_callers()` returns file paths, and `test_every_module_that_checks_for_an_agent_is_named_by_a_row` subtracts every path already named in `S.marker_modules()`. If a new refusal site is added inside a file that is already listed for a different verb, `unlisted` remains empty even though no row names the new refusal site. Example: add `agent_marker(...)` for a new verb in `ddflow/services/approvals/sites.py` or any already-row-listed module; the test passes, violating the stated “a refusal site cannot appear unlisted” purpose.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_sites.py:30

chunk_findings.detail: The `CALL` regex requires the marker name and `(` to be immediately adjacent, but Python permits whitespace between a function object and `(`. A newly added module containing `if agent_marker (a):` is a real call that `_callers()` will not detect, so the completeness test passes with an unlisted refusal site. The naive `line.split("#", 1)[0]` on line 22 similarly hides a real call after a `#` inside a string on the same line, e.g. `label = "#"; if agent_marker(a):`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_sites.py:13

chunk_findings.detail: `CALL.search(code)` is not token-aware, so string literals and docstrings containing `agent_marker(` count as callers. A row listing a module whose only occurrence is a docstring such as `"""Use agent_marker(x) here."""` will pass `test_every_listed_module_really_checks_and_exists` because that module appears in `_callers()`, even though the module does not actually check for an agent. This allows wrong rows to be accepted as valid.
